items.name: OpenAssistant/oasst1
items.about: Human-generated, human-annotated assistant conversations. The ready export contains 88,838 messages in 10,364 conversation trees and includes review, language, deletion, synthetic, PII, spam and quality fields.
items.screen: Streaming audit counts: 88,838 total; 37,836 satisfy English, nondeleted, reviewed, nonsynthetic, PII score <= 0 and spam score <= 0; 11,948 of those are assistant messages with quality >= 0.75; 5,515 also have rank 0. These are message counts, not dialogue counts or final training rows. Split by conversation tree before training.

items.name: google-research-datasets/Taskmaster TM-1
items.credit: Bill Byrne, Karthik Krishnamoorthi, Chinnadhurai Sankar, Arvind Neelakantan, Amit Dubey, Kyu-Young Kim, and Andy Cedilnik
items.about: 13,215 task-based dialogues across six service domains. Includes crowdsourced user and trained operator Wizard-of-Oz dialogues, plus self-dialogues written by crowdsourced workers. The source readme notes missing required fields in some otherwise retained dialogues and occasional transcription issues.
items.screen: Keep the source data unchanged. Use official self-dialog train/dev/test IDs when constructing splits; keep Wizard-of-Oz examples grouped by conversation ID. Do not treat the written self-dialog split as independently spoken interaction data.

items.name: Project-authored seed
items.about: Ten manually authored scenarios plus six deterministic templates with two substitutions each, covering objectives, constraints, missing information, correction, interruption, compaction, evidence, verification, ordinary conversation and short prose.
items.screen: All constructed scenarios are marked synthetic in curated output. Controlled substitutions are deterministic and human-authored; no model-generated answers are admitted.

policy: Raw source files are retained unchanged under the ignored data directory. This manifest and the source documentation record provenance; the archives are not committed. Acquisition and license declarations do not by themselves establish privacy clearance or training suitability.
